FROM STEVE MARSH

Firstly, I must congratulate youon a very well produced
magazine. You have filled a gap
for the serious user that has
been around for a long time, andhas worsened since the demise ofZX Computing.

I am including a program on thiscartridge called 'zap', which isa (hopefully) easy to use ERASE
utility. (use line 9020 to
copy). It takes all the hard
slog out of erasing unwanted
files. I would like to point outthat the program uses the '#14
to z$' routine contained in
A.Pennell's book 'Mastering yourZX Microdrive', and that the

program is already available on
the Gnome at Home BB and
Prestel.

The above book is well worth
reading and is an invaluable
reference guide.

How can we improve OUTLET?

It is early days yet, but the
initial signs have been
promising. Every magazine
suffers to some extent from lackof content to begin with, but
already you seem to be getting
willing contributors.

I hope that we, the readers do
not let you down after such a
promising start - so if you

haven't written yet, please try!

A magazine on two carts sounds agreat idea; I will certainly buyboth if you ever produce one!

The only gripe that I have is
JIGBLOX. Am I the only reader
who finds this puzzle boring?
The first was OK, but after thatthe novelty has worn off. Given
the shortage of space, I would
have thought that you might havemore interesting items instead.

Sorry to have taken up so much
space, but I have just one more
thing to say:

KEEP UP THE GOOD WORK!!

Steve Marsh

FROM BRIAN TO STEVE MARSH

Thanks Steve. I'll put 'Zap' in
a future issue - I did a lot of
soul-searching as to whether we
should use Andy Pennell's code.
According to his book it's O.K.
- with his permission. However,
not knowing how to contact him Ithink if we just credit him it
should be alright. Normally,
direct copies of listings from
books or magazines can't be usedin OUTLET so I don't want to
encourage anyone else.

Anyway, you've used the routine
to very good effect in your
program - I like the display
etc.

Only one gripe? - Can't be bad!
Yes, I know what you mean about
JIG!BLOX. We may well phase it
out in a few months. What do
others think?

             - Brian

FROM MR. G.A. MATTHEWS

I READ THE LETTER ABOUT
MEGABASIC WITH INTEREST. IT IS AGOOD UTILITY BUT WARN YOUR
SUBSCRIBERS IT PROBABLY WILL NOTWORK ON A PLUS 2 AT LEAST IT
WON'T ON MINE OR THE LAD AROUND
THE CORNERS, IT WILL WORK ON THESINCLAIR 128 48K MODE ONLY AND
ON THE 48K SPECTRUMS.

MEGABASIC COMES WITH A GOOD UDG
DESIGNER, YOU CAN DO PROCEDURES.I AGREE THERE IS LITTLE YOU CAN
DO WITH PROCEDURES THAT YOU
CANNOT ACHIEVE WITH SINCLAIR
BASIC. MEGABASIC DISABLES ALL
THE SINGLE ENTRY KEYWORDS SO YOUHAVE TO TYPE IN THE INSTRUCTIONSIN FULL,SAY LIKE A REAL COMPUTERCOME BACK 48K ALL IS FORGIVEN.

I ENCLOSE ON THE REST OF THE

VERY SHORT BASIC ROUTINE, WOT,
DRAWS A VERY COLOURFUL SERIES OFPATTERNS, THE NEXT IS A MACHINE
CODE ROUTINE MICRODRIVE
CONVERTER, MDC, LOCATED AT
65200,136. WHEN CALLED IT WILL
RUN THROUGH ANY BASIC PROGRAM INTHE MEMORY CHANGING LOAD AND
SAVE ETC. TO MICRODRIVE SYNTAX.

TRANSFERRING SOMETHING LIKE
TASWORD 2 FROM TAPE TO DRIVE.
THE LAST IS ONLY MY FAVOURITE
COPY TO PRINTER ROUTINE. ONE
THAT ACTUALLY WORKS WITH MY GLP
AN AWKWARD LITTLE BEAST!

G.A. MATTHEWS

TO MR. G.A. MATTHEWS FROM BRIAN

I'm quite partial to silly
programs.'WOT' I may get in thisissue, if not then next issue.
In your covering letter you say
the microdrive convertor is froma magazine listing so we can't
put it in OUTLET. The screen
copier wouldn't work for me.
What baud rate are you using? Bythe way, if you use JOTTER, can
you space your DATA lines out -
line 10, line 20 instead of
lines 1,2,3 - it helps me a lot
with the editing. Also - our
text compressor only works with
lower case so we don't save any
memory with CAPITAL letters!
Nag, Nag, Nag...  Thanks for theMEGABASIC info - Brian

From: Mr. Norman Unitt

   Hello again!   For some time
I have used my Spectrum to keep
a close watch on all my
household expenditure.

  As always it is worked around
my HR-5 printer so that I can
print out a total account and
see how the expenditure is
going.

   Lines 8000 onwards contain
the necessary DIM statements andDATA to initialise the system.

   The headings can be amended
before initilisation in this
area or they can be altered
during run time from the menu.

   The amend menu also caters
for any alteration in the
figures. It alters all relevent
sub-totals and Grand Total
automatically.

Oh dear, Oh dear, received this
morning one nicely formatted buttotally blank cartridge, which
is returned herewith.

Yours sincerely,

Norman Unitt

TO: NORMAN UNITT FROM RON

Dear Norman,

Ouch!

How could I possibly send you a
blank cartridge instead of issue
004 of OUTLET! It was there all
the time written in invisible
ink - all you needed to do was
warm it in the oven for 20
minutes and all the text would
have appeared as if by magic.

Please find enclosed a pre-
warmed copy which should solve
the problem. (Actually, it's a
wonder you didn't get my
brief-case - I've been stuffing
that many black rectangular
things into envelopes lately!)

Many thanks for your
contribution, I've only had time
for a swift glance but it looks
as though I'll be sending you a
cheque for this as soon as we
can get it into OUTLET.

Regards,

Ron Cavers




[The program: "EXPEND" referred

appear in the next issue - BC]

From Brian Gaff

Hi There! Thanks for including
my M/drive tips in the December
issue! I am afraid I have not
fixed 'Compexpand' yet! I do not
seem to have enough hours these
days! Re: HiSoft BASIC, it needs
more work on your programs as it
does not support the SAVE/LOAD &
certain other commands.BLAST was
not as bad as some reviews made
out actually! It was very long
though & always included ALL the
"runtimes" [supporting code
routines - BC], unlike Hisoft.
It was a pain to use from tape
too! I have about 10 programs

It is best to resave the
programs as CODE though as the

Re the CliveCopy (as I know it!)
I wish I had thought of that
too! I Multifaced mine to get
around it! The +3 disc next, it
CANNOT be used from 48K mode as
it has disabled paging! I think
you could do it if you went
into 48K mode without disabling
it... how I do not know. You
would then need to rewrite the
disc calling routines! You have
no way back!If anyone knows of a
fiddle, I would be interested. I
have a problem on the +3 just
now! I have put SCRABBLE
(original), on disk. It crashes
on return to BASIC to "SAVE a
game" ONLY after a few words are
on the board! Weird...

       - Brian Gaff

To Brian Gaff from Brian Cavers

Thanks Brian. Don't worry about
COMPEXPAND too much. I know what
you mean about not enough hours
in the day! As for BLAST - I
wonder if there were different
versions out? [THIS IS THE BLAST
YOUR BASIC COMPILER NOT BLAST IT
THE TASWORD DISPLAY IN THIS
ISSUE! - B.C. [What's this? Are
you editing your own letters
now? - B.C.[Schizophrenic? who's
schizophrenic?-B.C.] ] ]

Well,one more nail in the coffin
of a +3 OUTLET!
                - Brian Cavers

From: Mike Haine

  Hi Ron! Thanks for no.3. It is
well up to scratch. We seem to
be fated to cross swords (in
friendly combat!). It is on the
subject of HEX this time. By now
I hope you will have read my bit
on 'Numbers', sent to you last
month. [This is planned as an
"OUTCLASS" article next issue -
B.C.] If so you will see how the
unique relationship between Hex
and Binary makes the use of the
former almost essential in
writing and understanding m/c.

Just as a simple example if you
use the opcodes to load a number
into the double register,such as
Ld HL,13724, you have no ready

idea of the values in the single
registers H & L. If you use the
hex notation Ld HL,359Ch, you
know that H will hold 35h & L,
9Ch.I do agree that at first
sight Hex seems unnecessary but
as one gets to the more
sophisticated aspects of m/c it
is difficult to see how one
could do without it. It is
unlucky that we didn't have 16
fingers in the first place. It
would have made things much
easier all round. The decimal
system is really not at all the
best one to have chosen.

 PRINTING OUTLOOK. Some time ago
on MICRONET, I tried to raise
some interest in the idea of
distributing a magazine via

Prestel and printing it in the
home. The response to the idea,
as usual on the NET, was minimal
and I gave it up. I had
developed some m/c print progs.
which would drive a full sized
printer to print 3 Prestel
frames (each 24 lines, 40 char/
line) across an A4 sheet, or 12
frames on one sheet, complete
with Prestel graphics and non-
stop at full printer speed. It
would also be possible to trans-
mit,with the text, info to
determine the print layout. The
same sort of thing could be done
with OUTLOOK. The distribution
would remain the same but some
printer progs. could be provided
to print out the text in 4
columns (or perhaps 2 cols.of 64
char.lines)

Graphics and diagrams could be
included. It does seem to me
that this would be an exciting
and worthwhile project and which
I should personally welcome the
chance to help on. ANY INTEREST!
I suppose a lot would depend on
how many subscribers have full
sized dot matrix printers. How
about a questionnaire?

        Mike Haine.

To: Mike Haine from Brian

Ron and I are in complete agree-
ment on HEX! - We both started
to look into machine code, I
reckon, about 3 years ago and
started to really write code
routines about a year or so
later so I would say we've been
writing code for nearly a couple
of years. Certainly, I now
regularly write routines on a
monthly basis for OUTLET. As an
example, JIG!BLOX has to scroll
different sized areas of both
the display file and the
attribute file from anywhere on
the screen, up, down, left and
right. There are sound routines,
more recently the ON ERROR GO TO
microdrive routines in this

issue, text compression, screen
compression, graphic handling
and much more - in short, quite
a variety. In all this time we
have never found any use for HEX
- on the contrary - it has been
a serious hindrance and a
frustration. The few times I've
made notes in binary to try to
visualise what is happening in a
routine, HEX was not needed.

I'm prepared to provisionally
accept that, as you say, "as one
gets to the more sophisticated
aspects of m/c" it may have use
on occasion but then why not
reserve it for those few
occasions? As it is it pervades
even the most trivial listings
for no purpose. Perhaps in

another 5 years of programming I
may find some use for it now and
again but for now I'm enjoying
myself with what I know and
understand. Don't get me wrong -
I'm quite familiar with what HEX
is - I did my homework 3 years
ago - but I've never been a
follower of the herd - I think
for myself and until someone can
actually DEMONSTRATE the value
of HEX to me, not just talk
about it, then I use my highest
judgement in the light of my own
experience.

I might add to anyone reading
this who would like to "get
started" in machine code, you
must decide for yourself. I can
only tell you FOR CERTAIN that I

have written many PRACTICAL,
USEFUL, routines - as you can
see in the running of OUTLET,
without using HEX. Although I
would recommend you at least
read the basic theory of what
HEX is, (read Mike Haine's
OUTCLASS article in the next
issue which is first class on
the subject!), in my opinion and
experience you can go quite a
long way without it. (All I need
now is my ON ERROR routines to
go wrong and I'll have egg on my
face!).

Phew! Next subject! I definitely
like your PRINT routines, Mike.
I'm not sure how to integrate it
into OUTLET though. Remember,
all our text is compressed -

there just would not be room for
normal text. I assume your text
would include various flags
which would clash with ours. Can
the text be displayed on screen
for those without printers? If
you can send in a demo of some
kind - say the driving software
and supporting BASIC plus an
article of some kind we'll
certainly include it as an
experiment then we may be better
able to assess how to approach
the matter. Meanwhile, I'd be
grateful if readers would write
in with comments on this.

I can't help feeling your idea
is good enough to set up a
magazine of your own based on
printed copy like a newsletter

but transmitted by disc or even
cassette. I'm not certain
whether it can be patched on to
OUTLET though. I visualize
OUTLET as an ON-SCREEN dynamic
mixture of programs and text
interacting with the drive - the
printer routines being added for
convenience to dump the odd item
for ready reference. However,
let's lean in your direction
with a trial, if possible, and
see if readership response will
pull us completely over.

                   - Brian

From: Mr. E.M. DUFFIELD

Dear OUTLET,

Thank you very much for Issue
#3. It really is excellent. The
news very interesting and the
graphics are marvellous,
especially as the Spectrum only
uses half the screen.

In the past I spent quite a lot
of time looking for the bug in
the Shadow ROM that causes the
RS232 to malfunction when
receiving data. It works
perfectly when sending to
printer but when receiving it
will likely as not give the
wrong character code or none at
all.

The bug is at location 3023 in
the shadow ROM. the instruction
JR 3056 should be JR 3062. I'm
now able to use an EP44 keyboard
to type this via Tasword II. The
only place I could find to patch
in the code was at the bottom of
the Help Page. I mention all
this as I would be interested if
any other of your readers have
found a use for the RS232 port.

I notice your dislike of HEX so
have used decimal numbers.

It appears that the expansion
memory chips are hard to locate.
They are the eight chips,arrang-
ed in two rows of eight. Data
line 7 is the top left hand side
one. The top row runs 7-6-5-4

and the bottom row 3-2-1-0.

Thanking you once again.

E.M. DUFFIELD


Thanks for that info. Am I right
in thinking that you have an
"external" keyboard which passes
keypress data to the Spectrum
via the I'face 1 RS232 port, by-
passing the shadow ROM routine
but driven by your own routine
stored in memory at the place
where TASWORD II stores its HELP
PAGE and that you can thereby
type into TASWORD II?AH!-Just on
the phone to Ron who says he has
received a routine from you that
may be the very code! That may
confirm it.         - Brian

From: David Gent

 Dear Ron & Brian,

 Having received my copy of
'OUTLET' and running through it,
I thought - at last, a magazine
that does not treat you like a
games playing Moron.

 With useful routines and
interesting articles, you are
certainly on to a winner.

 For too long now, the Micro-
Drive user has been neglected.

 In fact, so impressive is this
effort, that you will find
enclosed my subscription for one
year.

 Now that the grovelling is out
of the way, (although it was all
meant), I have a couple of
points that you may be able to
help me with.

 First, after reading that you
are thinking of bringing out a
2 M/D version of Outlet, what
will happen when I have only
subscribed for 12 of the single
cartridge versions, as I would
not wish to miss out on any
further developments of your
magazine.

 Next, I have recently been
looking for a Teletext Adapter
for my 128K Spectrum, (Sinclair
not Amstrad +2), and have been
told that the Volex model can

work with my computer, but
depending on which model of
adapter you get. If you or your
readers can help, either with
advice or an adapter that is
compatible with the 128 Spectrum
for sale, then I would be most
grateful.

 Now here are a couple of tips,
as I understand you are looking
for an ON ERROR GOTO function, I
suggest you have a look at
'Master Your ZX Microdrive', by
Andrew Pennell, published by
Sunshine books, as he lists not
only this type of routine, but
also an ON End Of File GOTO
routine, along with a few more
routines I have found
invaluable.

 Next, to save memory, in Basic
programs, use terms such as NOT
PI for 0, or PI/PI for 1, INT PI
for 3, and using VAL"number",
because of the way the Spectrum
stores numbers, this can save
upto 5 bytes per number. As this
will slow the program down, it
ends up as a balancing act
between speed and the amount of
capacity you wish to save on the
cartridge.

 Lastly, you will also find on
my cartridge a small program
describing an idea I had for
making a M/D storage box, I hope
you find it helpful.[Yes! I have
extracted this and will put it
in separately or in the next
issue - B.C.]

 Keep up the good work.

             Yours,

           David Gent.

To: David Gent from Brian

Thanks David. I've just been
searching for some info on the
Volex adaptor but couldn't find
it. Can anyone else help? If I
find any info during the next
week or so I'll put it in the
next issue.

Thanks for the memory saving
info- We do use those techniques
- see OUTCLASS this month.

To upgrade your subscription to
a two-cartridge subscription:

1. Calculate what  the remainder
of your present sub is WORTH  by
dividing the total cost by total
months and  multiplying  by  the
months left.

2. Calculate what the remainder
WOULD be worth at the  new  rate
(see form)  following  the  same
formula.

3. Subtract the two (round it
down to the nearest pound) and
just send the difference with a
note to us of what you want.

We've put a  little  program  in
this issue called SUBCALC  which
can work it out automatically.
Anybody in doubt - just write in
and say what you want. We'll
first of all make sure you get a
double cartridge and don't miss
anything. Then we'll work it out
and tell you the difference and
you can send it next time. O.K.?

Yes, We managed to borrow a copy
of Andy Pennell's "MASTER YOUR
ZX MICRODRIVE". I've spent long
hours wrestling with the ON
ERROR GO TO routine and think I
have grasped the essence of it.
I've now written my own routine
which is running the microdrive
version of this issue to handle
the two cartridges. Next issue I
hope to include it as a separate
utility.
                  - Brian.

ОТ STEVE MARSH

Прежде всего, я должен
поздравить вас с прекрасно
сделанным журналом. Вы закрыли
брешь для серьезных
пользователей, которая зевала
уже давно и стала лишь хуже
после кончины ZX Computing.

Я прилагаю на этом картридже
программу 'zap', которая
(надеюсь) проста в обращении:
это утилита для ERASE (для

9020). Она берет на себя всю
рутину по удалению ненужных

программа использует процедуру
'#14 to z$' из книги
A.Pennell 'Mastering your
ZX Microdrive', и эта

программа уже доступна на
Gnome at Home BB и Prestel.

Вышеупомянутую книгу определенно
стоит прочесть, это бесценное
справочное руководство.

Как нам улучшить OUTLET?

Пока еще самое начало, но
первые признаки многообещающи.
Каждый журнал поначалу в той или
иной степени страдает от
нехватки материалов, но у вас
уже появились желающие писать.

Надеюсь, что мы, читатели,
не подведем вас после столь
обнадеживающего старта — так что
если вы еще не написали,

пожалуйста, попробуйте!

Журнал на двух картриджах
звучит как отличная идея; я
непременно куплю оба, если вы
когда-нибудь такой выпустите!

Единственное нарекание — это
JIGBLOX. Неужели я единственный
читатель, считающий эту
головоломку скучной? Первая была
еще ничего, но затем эффект
новизны пропал. Учитывая дефицит
места, я полагал, что вместо нее
могли бы быть вещи поинтереснее.

Прошу прощения, что занял так
много места, но мне осталось
сказать лишь одно:

ТАК ДЕРЖАТЬ!!

Steve Marsh

ОТ BRIAN ДЛЯ STEVE MARSH

Спасибо, Steve. Я включу 'Zap'
в один из будущих номеров — я
долго колебался насчет того,
можем ли мы использовать код
Andy Pennell. Судя по его книге,
все в порядке — но с его
разрешения. Впрочем, не зная,
как с ним связаться, полагаю,
что если мы просто укажем
авторство, этого хватит. Обычно
прямые копии листингов из книг
или журналов не могут быть
использованы в OUTLET, поэтому я
не хочу поощрять остальных.

Как бы то ни было, вы очень
удачно применили эту процедуру
в своей программе — мне
понравился экран и т.д.

Всего одно нарекание? — Не так
уж плохо! Да, я понимаю, о чем
вы по поводу JIG!BLOX. Мы вполне
можем свернуть ее через пару
месяцев. А что думают другие?

             - Brian

ОТ М-РА G.A. MATTHEWS

Я С ИНТЕРЕСОМ ПРОЧЕЛ ПИСЬМО О
MEGABASIC. ЭТО ХОРОШАЯ УТИЛИТА,
НО ПРЕДУПРЕДИТЕ ПОДПИСЧИКОВ, ЧТО
ОНА, ВЕРОЯТНО, НЕ БУДЕТ
РАБОТАТЬ НА PLUS 2 — ПО КРАЙНЕЙ
МЕРЕ, НЕ РАБОТАЕТ НА МОЕМ ИЛИ У
ПАРНЯ ЗА УГЛОМ; ОНА БУДЕТ
РАБОТАТЬ ТОЛЬКО В 48K-РЕЖИМЕ НА
SINCLAIR 128 И НА 48K SPECTRUM.

В КОМПЛЕКТЕ С MEGABASIC ИДЕТ

есть в наличии все мануалы для
Sinclair/Amstrad. Стоит
попробовать: 0772 555 034
                - Brian.

От: David Gent

 Дорогие Ron & Brian!

 Получив свой экземпляр 'OUTLET'
и пробежавшись по нему, я
подумал: наконец-то журнал,
который не держит тебя за
играющего в игрушки недоумка.

 С полезными процедурами и
интересными статьями вы
определенно обречены на успех.

 Слишком долго пользователи
Microdrive оставались без
внимания.

 На самом деле эта работа
настолько впечатляет, что вы
найдёте внутри мою подписку на
один год.

 Теперь, когда с дифирамбами
покончено (хотя всё было от
чистого сердца), у меня есть пара
вопросов, с которыми вы,
возможно, сможете мне помочь.

 Во-первых, прочитав о том, что
вы подумываете выпустить версию
Outlet на 2 M/D, что произойдёт,
если я подписался только на 12
выпусков в версии на одном
картридже? Ведь мне не хотелось
бы пропустить дальнейшее
развитие вашего журнала.

 Далее, я недавно искал
адаптер Teletext для своего
Spectrum 128K (Sinclair, а не
Amstrad +2), и мне сказали, что
модель от Volex может

работать с моим компьютером, но
всё зависит от конкретной модели
адаптера. Если вы или ваши
читатели смогут помочь — советом
или продажей адаптера,
совместимого со Spectrum 128, я
буду крайне признателен.

 А теперь пара советов:
насколько я понимаю, вы ищете
функцию ON ERROR GOTO. Советую
вам взглянуть на книгу «Master
Your ZX Microdrive» Эндрю
Пеннелла (Andrew Pennell),
выпущенную Sunshine books. Там
приведена не только процедура
такого типа, но и процедура
ON End Of File GOTO, а также ещё
несколько процедур, которые я
нашёл бесценными.

 Затем, для экономии памяти в
программах на Basic используйте
выражения вроде NOT PI вместо 0,
или PI/PI вместо 1, INT PI
вместо 3, а также VAL"число" —
из-за того, как Spectrum
хранит числа, это может
сэкономить до 5 байт на число.
Поскольку это замедлит
программу, всё сводится к
балансированию между скоростью и
объёмом места, которое вы хотите
сберечь на картридже.

 Наконец, на моём картридже вы
также найдёте небольшую
программу с описанием моей идеи
по созданию коробки для хранения
M/D, надеюсь, она вам пригодится.
[Да! Я извлёк её и помещу
отдельно или в следующем номере
— B.C.]

 Продолжайте в том же духе.

             Искренне ваш,

Для: David Gent от Brian

Спасибо, Дэвид. Я тут как раз
искал информацию по адаптеру
Volex, но ничего не нашёл. Может
ли кто-то ещё помочь? Если я
найду какие-нибудь сведения в
течение ближайшей недели или
около того, помещу их в
следующий номер.

Спасибо за совет по экономии
памяти — мы используем эти
приёмы, см. OUTCLASS в этом
месяце.

Чтобы перевести вашу подписку
на формат двух картриджей:

1. Посчитайте, СКОЛЬКО СТОИТ
остаток вашей текущей подписки:
разделите общую стоимость на
общее число месяцев и умножьте на
количество оставшихся месяцев.

2. Посчитайте, сколько остаток
СТОИЛ БЫ по новому тарифу (см.
бланк) по той же формуле.

3. Вычтите одно из другого
(округлите в меньшую сторону до
ближайшего фунта) и просто
пришлите разницу с запиской о
том, что именно вам нужно.

Мы поместили в этот номер
небольшую программу SUBCALC,
которая может посчитать всё
автоматически. Если кто-то
сомневается — просто напишите и
сообщите, чего вы хотите.
Первым делом мы позаботимся о
том, чтобы вы получили двойной
картридж и ничего не пропустили.
Затем мы всё посчитаем, сообщим
вам разницу, и вы сможете
прислать её в следующий раз.
Договорились?
Да, нам удалось одолжить
экземпляр книги Andy Pennell
"MASTER YOUR ZX MICRODRIVE".
Я провёл долгие часы, сражаясь
с процедурой ON ERROR GO TO,
и думаю, что уловил её суть.
Теперь я написал свою
собственную процедуру, которая
управляет микродрайвной версией
этого выпуска для работы
с двумя картриджами. В следующем
номере надеюсь включить её
как отдельную утилиту.
                  - Brian.

### FROM STEVE MARSH

Firstly, I must congratulate you on a very well produced magazine. You have filled a gap for the serious user that has been around for a long time, and has worsened since the demise of ZX Computing.

I am including a program on this cartridge called 'zap', which is a (hopefully) easy to use ERASE utility. (use line 9020 to copy). It takes all the hard slog out of erasing unwanted files. I would like to point out that the program uses the '#14 to z$' routine contained in A.Pennell's book 'Mastering your ZX Microdrive', and that the program is already available on the Gnome at Home BB and Prestel.

The above book is well worth reading and is an invaluable reference guide.

How can we improve OUTLET?

It is early days yet, but the initial signs have been promising. Every magazine suffers to some extent from lack of content to begin with, but already you seem to be getting willing contributors.

I hope that we, the readers do not let you down after such a promising start - so if you haven't written yet, please try!

A magazine on two carts sounds a great idea; I will certainly buy both if you ever produce one!

The only gripe that I have is JIGBLOX. Am I the only reader who finds this puzzle boring? The first was OK, but after that the novelty has worn off. Given the shortage of space, I would have thought that you might have more interesting items instead.

Sorry to have taken up so much space, but I have just one more thing to say:

KEEP UP THE GOOD WORK!!

Steve Marsh

### FROM BRIAN TO STEVE MARSH

Thanks Steve. I'll put 'Zap' in a future issue - I did a lot of soul-searching as to whether we should use Andy Pennell's code. According to his book it's O.K. - with his permission. However, not knowing how to contact him I think if we just credit him it should be alright. Normally, direct copies of listings from books or magazines can't be used in OUTLET so I don't want to encourage anyone else.

Anyway, you've used the routine to very good effect in your program - I like the display etc.

Only one gripe? - Can't be bad! Yes, I know what you mean about JIG!BLOX. We may well phase it out in a few months. What do others think?

— Brian

### FROM MR. G.A. MATTHEWS

I READ THE LETTER ABOUT MEGABASIC WITH INTEREST. IT IS A GOOD UTILITY BUT WARN YOUR SUBSCRIBERS IT PROBABLY WILL NOT WORK ON A PLUS 2 AT LEAST IT WON'T ON MINE OR THE LAD AROUND THE CORNERS, IT WILL WORK ON THE SINCLAIR 128 48K MODE ONLY AND ON THE 48K SPECTRUMS.

WHEN CALLED IT WILL RUN THROUGH ANY BASIC PROGRAM IN THE MEMORY CHANGING LOAD AND SAVE ETC. TO MICRODRIVE SYNTAX. SAVES A LOT OF TYPING IF TRANSFERRING SOMETHING LIKE TASWORD 2 FROM TAPE TO DRIVE. ### From: Mr. Norman Unitt

Hello again! For some time I have used my Spectrum to keep a close watch on all my household expenditure.

### From Brian Gaff

Hi There! Thanks for including my M/drive tips in the December issue! I am afraid I have not fixed 'Compexpand' yet! I do not seem to have enough hours these days! ### To Brian Gaff from Brian Cavers

Thanks Brian. Don't worry about COMPEXPAND too much. I know what you mean about not enough hours in the day! As for BLAST - I wonder if there were different versions out? [THIS IS THE BLAST YOUR BASIC COMPILER NOT BLAST IT THE TASWORD DISPLAY IN THIS ISSUE! - B.C. [What's this? Are you editing your own letters now? - B.C. [Schizophrenic? who's schizophrenic?-B.C.] ] ]

### From: Mike Haine

Hi Ron! Thanks for no.3. It is well up to scratch. We seem to be fated to cross swords (in friendly combat!). It is on the subject of HEX this time. By now I hope you will have read my bit on 'Numbers', sent to you last month. [This is planned as an "OUTCLASS" article next issue - B.C.] If so you will see how the unique relationship between Hex and Binary makes the use of the former almost essential in writing and understanding m/c.

Just as a simple example if you use the opcodes to load a number into the double register, such as Ld HL,13724, you have no ready

...idea of the values in the single registers H & L. If you use the hex notation `Ld HL,359Ch`, you know that H will hold 35h & L, 9Ch. I do agree that at first sight Hex seems unnecessary but as one gets to the more sophisticated aspects of m/c it is difficult to see how one could do without it. It is unlucky that we didn't have 16 fingers in the first place. It would have made things much easier all round. The decimal system is really not at all the best one to have chosen.

**PRINTING OUTLOOK.** Some time ago on MICRONET, I tried to raise some interest in the idea of distributing a magazine via Prestel and printing it in the home. The response to the idea, as usual on the NET, was minimal and I gave it up. I had developed some m/c print progs. which would drive a full sized printer to print 3 Prestel frames (each 24 lines, 40 char/line) across an A4 sheet, or 12 frames on one sheet, complete with Prestel graphics and non-stop at full printer speed. It would also be possible to transmit, with the text, info to determine the print layout. The same sort of thing could be done with OUTLOOK. The distribution would remain the same but some printer progs. could be provided to print out the text in 4 columns (or perhaps 2 cols. of 64 char. lines).

Graphics and diagrams could be included. It does seem to me that this would be an exciting and worthwhile project and which I should personally welcome the chance to help on. ANY INTEREST! I suppose a lot would depend on how many subscribers have full sized dot matrix printers. How about a questionnaire?

Mike Haine.

---

### To: Mike Haine from Brian

Ron and I are in complete agreement on HEX! — We both started to look into machine code, I reckon, about 3 years ago and started to really write code routines about a year or so later so I would say we've been writing code for nearly a couple of years. Certainly, I now regularly write routines on a monthly basis for OUTLET. As an example, JIG!BLOX has to scroll different sized areas of both the display file and the attribute file from anywhere on the screen, up, down, left and right. There are sound routines, more recently the ON ERROR GO TO microdrive routines in this issue, text compression, screen compression, graphic handling and much more — in short, quite a variety. In all this time we have never found any use for HEX — on the contrary — it has been a serious hindrance and a frustration. The few times I've made notes in binary to try to visualise what is happening in a routine, HEX was not needed.

I'm prepared to provisionally accept that, as you say, "as one gets to the more sophisticated aspects of m/c" it may have use on occasion but then why not reserve it for those few occasions? As it is it pervades even the most trivial listings for no purpose. Perhaps in another 5 years of programming I may find some use for it now and again but for now I'm enjoying myself with what I know and understand. Don't get me wrong — I'm quite familiar with what HEX is — I did my homework 3 years ago — but I've never been a follower of the herd — I think for myself and until someone can actually DEMONSTRATE the value of HEX to me, not just talk about it, then I use my highest judgement in the light of my own experience.

I might add to anyone reading this who would like to "get started" in machine code, you must decide for yourself. I can only tell you FOR CERTAIN that I have written many PRACTICAL, USEFUL, routines — as you can see in the running of OUTLET, without using HEX. Although I would recommend you at least read the basic theory of what HEX is, (read Mike Haine's OUTCLASS article in the next issue which is first class on the subject!), in my opinion and experience you can go quite a long way without it. (All I need now is my ON ERROR routines to go wrong and I'll have egg on my face!).

Phew! Next subject! I definitely like your PRINT routines, Mike. I'm not sure how to integrate it into OUTLET though. Remember, all our text is compressed — there just would not be room for normal text. I assume your text would include various flags which would clash with ours. Can the text be displayed on screen for those without printers? If you can send in a demo of some kind — say the driving software and supporting BASIC plus an article of some kind we'll certainly include it as an experiment then we may be better able to assess how to approach the matter. Meanwhile, I'd be grateful if readers would write in with comments on this.

I can't help feeling your idea is good enough to set up a magazine of your own based on printed copy like a newsletter but transmitted by disc or even cassette. I'm not certain whether it can be patched on to OUTLET though. I visualize OUTLET as an ON-SCREEN dynamic mixture of programs and text interacting with the drive — the printer routines being added for convenience to dump the odd item for ready reference. However, let's lean in your direction with a trial, if possible, and see if readership response will pull us completely over.

— Brian

### From: Mr. E.M. DUFFIELD

Dear OUTLET,

Thank you very much for Issue #3. It really is excellent. The news very interesting and the graphics are marvellous, especially as the Spectrum only uses half the screen.

In the past I spent quite a lot of time looking for the bug in the Shadow ROM that causes the RS232 to malfunction when receiving data. It works perfectly when sending to printer but when receiving it will likely as not give the wrong character code or none at all.

The bug is at location 3023 in the shadow ROM. The instruction `JR 3056` should be `JR 3062`. I'm now able to use an EP44 keyboard to type this via Tasword II. The only place I could find to patch in the code was at the bottom of the Help Page. I mention all this as I would be interested if any other of your readers have found a use for the RS232 port.

I notice your dislike of HEX so have used decimal numbers.

It appears that the expansion memory chips are hard to locate. They are the eight chips, arranged in two rows of eight. Data line 7 is the top left hand side one. The top row runs 7-6-5-4 and the bottom row 3-2-1-0.

Thanking you once again.

E.M. DUFFIELD

Thanks for that info. Am I right in thinking that you have an "external" keyboard which passes keypress data to the Spectrum via the I'face 1 RS232 port, bypassing the shadow ROM routine but driven by your own routine stored in memory at the place where TASWORD II stores its HELP PAGE and that you can thereby type into TASWORD II? AH! — Just on the phone to Ron who says he has received a routine from you that may be the very code! That may confirm it.

— Brian

### From: MR. G.A. MATTHEWS

Dear Sir,

Having run your first 3 issues of OUTLET I must say that I am very impressed.

May I make some comments! Re the letter from Mr. Nicholls, Issue 2. I bought LASER GENIUS. The monitor did not run. I too got no response from OCEAN. I have persuaded the lot to work. If Mr. Nicholls wants a copy of the assembler file handler or monitor let him have my phone number: 01 594 1165.

I have a spare 128 hand book if Mr. Clapham, Issue 3 wants it. Phone 01 594 1165.

Now, if anyone out there has a working copy of the LASER BASIC SPRITE GENERATOR program — I bought LASER BASIC — One side of the tape works, side 2 does not. Writing to OCEAN is a waste of paper.

G.A. MATTHEWS

That's marvellous! Thanks! See what happens when you create an OUTLET? — Something starts to pour...

Talking of hand books I have a phone number jotted down which I think I saw on Micronet. I think it is the Amstrad number who stock all the Sinclair/Amstrad manuals. It's worth trying: 0772 555 034

— Brian.

### From: David Gent

Dear Ron & Brian,

Having received my copy of 'OUTLET' and running through it, I thought — at last, a magazine that does not treat you like a games playing Moron.

With useful routines and interesting articles, you are certainly on to a winner.

For too long now, the Micro-Drive user has been neglected.

In fact, so impressive is this effort, that you will find enclosed my subscription for one year.

Now that the grovelling is out of the way, (although it was all meant), I have a couple of points that you may be able to help me with.

First, after reading that you are thinking of bringing out a 2 M/D version of Outlet, what will happen when I have only subscribed for 12 of the single cartridge versions, as I would not wish to miss out on any further developments of your magazine.

Next, I have recently been looking for a Teletext Adapter for my 128K Spectrum, (Sinclair not Amstrad +2), and have been told that the Volex model can work with my computer, but depending on which model of adapter you get. If you or your readers can help, either with advice or an adapter that is compatible with the 128 Spectrum for sale, then I would be most grateful.

Now here are a couple of tips, as I understand you are looking for an ON ERROR GOTO function, I suggest you have a look at 'Master Your ZX Microdrive', by Andrew Pennell, published by Sunshine books, as he lists not only this type of routine, but also an ON End Of File GOTO routine, along with a few more routines I have found invaluable.

Next, to save memory, in Basic programs, use terms such as NOT PI for 0, or PI/PI for 1, INT PI for 3, and using VAL"number", because of the way the Spectrum stores numbers, this can save upto 5 bytes per number. As this will slow the program down, it ends up as a balancing act between speed and the amount of capacity you wish to save on the cartridge.

Lastly, you will also find on my cartridge a small program describing an idea I had for making a M/D storage box, I hope you find it helpful. [Yes! I have extracted this and will put it in separately or in the next issue - B.C.]

Keep up the good work.

Yours,  
David Gent.

---

### To: David Gent from Brian

Thanks David. I've just been searching for some info on the Volex adaptor but couldn't find it. Can anyone else help? If I find any info during the next week or so I'll put it in the next issue.

Thanks for the memory saving info - We do use those techniques - see OUTCLASS this month.

To upgrade your subscription to a two-cartridge subscription:

1. Calculate what the remainder of your present sub is WORTH by dividing the total cost by total months and multiplying by the months left.
2. Calculate what the remainder WOULD be worth at the new rate (see form) following the same formula.
3. Subtract the two (round it down to the nearest pound) and just send the difference with a note to us of what you want.

We've put a little program in this issue called SUBCALC which can work it out automatically. Anybody in doubt - just write in and say what you want. We'll first of all make sure you get a double cartridge and don't miss anything. Then we'll work it out and tell you the difference and you can send it next time. O.K.?

Yes, We managed to borrow a copy of Andy Pennell's "MASTER YOUR ZX MICRODRIVE". I've spent long hours wrestling with the ON ERROR GO TO routine and think I have grasped the essence of it. I've now written my own routine which is running the microdrive version of this issue to handle the two cartridges. Next issue I hope to include it as a separate utility.

\- Brian.

### ОТ STEVE MARSH

Прежде всего, я должен поздравить вас с прекрасно сделанным журналом. Вы закрыли брешь для серьезных пользователей, которая зевала уже давно и стала лишь хуже после кончины ZX Computing.

Как нам улучшить OUTLET?
